correctness.rationale: The white-profile argument proves that any zero forcing set leaves at most two whites. Two whites in one part cannot force, and two whites in distinct singleton parts also cannot force; every other cross-part pair is forced in two steps. This gives the exact minimum sets, excludes larger inclusion-minimal sets, and yields the star-center irrelevance criterion. Fresh exhaustive simulation through order nine reproduced the full classification for all 87 multipartite isomorphism types tested. The repaired RESULT preserves this proof and changes the literature interpretation to acknowledge and correct the prior Proposition 3.2.

originality.rationale: Grood et al. already state that every complete multipartite graph with at least two parts is well-forced, so that headline is prior-covered. However, their Proposition 3.2 proof asserts that any set omitting two vertices from different parts is zero forcing; this is false when both omitted parts are singletons. The repaired result explicitly acknowledges that prior theorem, corrects the singleton boundary, gives the exact minimal-set classification for every part profile, and derives the exact irrelevant-vertex classification. Those refinements are not supplied by the inspected prior sources.
residual_risks: A differently phrased earlier correction of Proposition 3.2 or an unindexed complete-multipartite minimal-set census could exist.

value.rationale: Correcting the boundary of a published family-level proposition and giving the exact minimal-set and irrelevant-vertex structure is mathematically useful: the singleton distinction changes which subsets are zero forcing, and the vertex classification answers a named structural question introduced in the same literature. The repaired presentation no longer claims novelty for the already-known well-forced conclusion.

final_claim: For connected complete multipartite graphs, the previously published well-forced conclusion remains true, but the exact minimal-set classification requires a singleton correction: in a noncomplete graph the minimal zero forcing sets are precisely complements of two vertices in distinct parts that are not both singleton, while complete graphs use one-vertex complements; the only zero-forcing-irrelevant vertex in this class is the center of a nontrivial star.
limitations: Well-forcedness of complete multipartite graphs was already stated by Grood et al. and is not claimed as new.
The repair changes literature/novelty framing but not the proved minimal-set theorem.
The independent finite replay through order nine is corroborative; the proof is all-order.
